data.narrative:
QuantumScape is a public-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Jagdeep Singh, Tim Holme, and Fritz Prinz, currently valued at $3.63B following $2B+ in total fundraising. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables: Enovix ($1.0B), Solid Power ($504M), and LanzaTech ($73M).

The peer-median method applies directly given the availability of public trading comps in the solid-state battery and carbon capture space. The median valuation across these three peers stands at $504M, with a range spanning $73M (LanzaTech floor) to $1.0B (Enovix ceiling). This method produces a single triangulation point of $504M. The analytical range, accounting for measurement uncertainty, extends from $428M (low) to $580M (high), centered on the $504M median.

The current market valuation of $3.63B substantially exceeds the peer-derived range, suggesting QuantumScape commands a material premium—approximately 620% above the median comparable. Key uncertainties include the adequacy of the 3-peer sample size for valuation precision, stage-specific execution risk relative to peers, and technology differentiation that may or may not justify the premium. A full valuation would require additional methods (DCF, revenue multiples where applicable) to triangulate, as the single-method approach here constrains analytical confidence.
